economics.ped-mcq-def.0007.all: When quantity demanded does not change at all whatever happens to price (PED = 0)

economics.pes-analyse-1.0005.all: Textiles: spare capacity, so output can rise quickly with price -> elastic. Cotton: harvested once a year, time to grow, so cannot respond quickly -> inelastic (short run); may store stocks.

economics.pes-analyse-2.0007.all: Land shortage, skilled labour shortage, slow planning -> long production time, so quantity supplied barely responds to 15% price rise -> inelastic; price rises further when demand rises.

economics.pes-assess-1.0002.all: Plan: spare capacity -> textiles elastic; rice one harvest -> inelastic SR; but textile capacity limited once full, need workers/materials; rice stocks can be stored, long run more land planted; judgement: textiles more responsive in SR.

economics.pes-assess-2.0003.all: Plan: rising demand with inelastic supply -> large price rises, small quantity increase; affordability, homelessness, renting; builders profit; long run supply more elastic; government planning reform; depends on demand trend.

economics.pes-define1.0006.all: Quantity supplied does not change whatever the price; PES = 0.

economics.pes-define2.0001.all: Responsiveness of quantity supplied to a change in price; %dQs / %dP.

economics.pes-describe.0007.all: With spare capacity firms can increase output quickly using idle resources when price rises, so quantity supplied rises proportionately more.

economics.pes-diagram.0016.all: Steep upward-sloping supply curve labelled S; P1 to P2 on price axis; Q1 to Q2 small increase, proportionately smaller than price rise.

economics.pes-explain.0017.all: Stocks can be released quickly to market when price rises (1), so quantity supplied responds quickly (1), making supply of Tamarind's winter coats more price elastic (1).

economics.pes-mcq-def.0006.all: When quantity supplied cannot change whatever the price (PES = 0)

economics.ppc-calc.0012.all: Fish falls 810-700=110 tonnes for 60 extra furniture; OC = 110 tonnes of fish (1.83 tonnes per item).

economics.ppc-define1.0001.all: Curve showing maximum combinations of two goods an economy can produce with all resources fully and efficiently used.

economics.ppc-define2.0004.all: Increase in productive potential of economy (1), shown by outward shift of PPC (1).

economics.ppc-diagram.0016.all: Draw PPC1 shifted outward parallel(ish) to right of original, labelled PPC1, with arrows showing outward shift.

economics.ppc-explain.0016.all: More capital goods increase productive capacity in future (1), so PPC shifts outward (1); Novaris can produce more of both goods later, though fewer consumer goods now (1).

economics.ppc-mcq-def.0003.all: A combination of goods outside the curve which cannot be produced with the current resources and technology

economics.price-analyse-1.0004.all: Supply shifts left (poor harvests), demand shifts right (emerging markets) -> both raise price, so large 75% rise; quantity effect ambiguous; inelastic supply amplifies.

economics.price-analyse-2.0003.all: Demand for flats up (migration of students/workers) -> D right; supply inelastic/limited (scarce land, higher costs shift S left) -> rents rise 19%.

economics.price-analyse-3.0003.all: Price CHF 447 set below equilibrium; Qd > Qs at that price -> excess demand; supply fixed in SR; resale near double shows willingness to pay much higher.

economics.price-assess-1.0003.all: Plan: stays high if demand keeps growing and supply constraints persist; falls if harvests recover, new planting, substitutes, demand falls at high prices; judgement depends on weather/time horizon.

economics.price-assess-2.0002.all: Plan: continued migration and scarce land -> rents keep rising; but high rents deter migrants, new building, government policy (rent controls, housing); depends on supply response.

economics.price-assess-3.0003.all: Plan: for - excess demand, higher revenue/profit, clears shortage, deters resellers; against - goodwill/reputation, fairness, temporary demand surge, supply increasing soon, competitors; judgement.

economics.price-calc.0004.all: At EUR9: Qs 500 - Qd 380 = excess supply of 120 T-shirts.
